rules: Do not implement cryptographic primitives inside Worldshepherd application code.
Prefer maintained protocol/library implementations with explicit interoperability tests.
Do not remove classical algorithms until the relevant protocol and counterparties support the migration path.
Treat long-retention confidentiality as higher priority because harvest-now-decrypt-later risk precedes cryptographically relevant quantum computers.

surfaces.quantum_exposure: key establishment and authentication depend on deployed TLS suite
surfaces.target: crypto-agile TLS stack with standards-supported PQ/hybrid migration when ecosystem-ready
supported PQ/hybrid SSH path; preserve break-glass interoperability

surfaces.quantum_exposure: public-key signatures if asymmetric JWT/OIDC signing is used
surfaces.target: crypto-agile issuer/verifier interfaces and PQ-capable standards as ecosystem support matures
ML-DSA or SLH-DSA where tooling and verifier support permit; retain algorithm identifiers
dual/hybrid provenance strategy once repository/tooling support is available

surfaces.quantum_exposure: key wrapping/establishment may be vulnerable even when bulk symmetric encryption remains adequate
surfaces.target: inventory retention horizon and migrate vulnerable public-key wrapping mechanisms

surfaces.quantum_exposure: credential custody is primarily an operational secret-management problem; transport still requires inventory
surfaces.target: environment/secret-store injection only; never persist provider tokens in evidence records
